run.question: In the elasticsearch index 'app-276-logs-9j2k4p7m', run a `terms: { level: ["ERROR", "FATAL"] }` query and tell me how many hits come back. If that returns zero, find the right field for log severity and re-run the query.

report.summary: The requested `terms: { level: ["ERROR","FATAL"] }` query on index `app-276-logs-9j2k4p7m` returns 0 hits, because that index has no `level` field at all: its mapping contains only `@timestamp` (date), `msg` (text), `severity_num` (integer) and `svc` (keyword). Severity is stored numerically in `severity_num`; re-running the same terms query as `{"terms":{"severity_num":[5,6]}}` returns 8 hits. The index holds 23 documents in total (all with `svc` = order-276, timestamps 2026-11-23T18:05:01Z to 18:08:10Z, entirely inside the 1-hour sampled window ending 2026-11-23T18:09:28Z), and a severity breakdown over the full authorized window shows exactly 10 docs at severity_num 3, 5 at 4, 6 at 5 and 2 at 6 — so the 8 error-level hits are 6 ERROR (severity_num 5) and 2 FATAL (severity_num 6). A text-content check on `msg` for the strings ERROR/FATAL independently matches the same 8 documents, confirming the numeric mapping. No fault, alert or impact analysis was requested or performed; the FATAL messages in the sample read "[FATAL] Disk full" and the ERROR messages "[ERROR] DB timeout", but these are observations in log content, not an investigated incident cause.

claims.text: Index `app-276-logs-9j2k4p7m` exists with health green, status open and docs.count 23 at query time.

The mapping of `app-276-logs-9j2k4p7m` defines only these properties: `@timestamp` (date), `msg` (text), `severity_num` (integer), `svc` (keyword). There is no `level` property, so the requested `terms` clause targets an unmapped field and matches nothing.
The literal query `{"terms":{"level":["ERROR","FATAL"]}}` on `app-276-logs-9j2k4p7m` returned total 0 (relation eq) with 0 shard failures in the sampled window 2026-11-23T17:09:28Z to 18:09:28Z.

The severity field actually used in the documents is `severity_num`: the query `{"terms":{"severity_num":[5,6]}}` on `app-276-logs-9j2k4p7m` returned total 8 (relation eq), 0 shard failures, over the sampled window ending 2026-11-23T18:09:28Z.

A terms aggregation on `severity_num` over the full authorized window gave buckets key 3 = 10 docs, key 4 = 5 docs, key 5 = 6 docs, key 6 = 2 docs (sum_other_doc_count 0), with total 23 docs and all `svc` = order-276; so the 8 error-level hits decompose as 6 at severity_num 5 and 2 at severity_num 6.

Document content confirms the numeric-to-name mapping: rows with `"msg":"[ERROR] DB timeout N"` carry `severity_num`: 5 and rows with `"msg":"[FATAL] Disk full N"` carry `severity_num`: 6; documents with severity_num 3 are `[INFO]` and 4 are `[WARN]`.
A text-level check on `msg` (bool should with `match: msg ERROR` or `match: msg FATAL`) returned total 8, matching the 8 hits from the `severity_num` terms query.

All 23 documents carry @timestamp between 2026-11-23T18:05:01Z and 2026-11-23T18:08:10Z, i.e. entirely inside the 1-hour sampled window used for both count queries, so the 0-hit and 8-hit results are not explained by the time filter.

Rejected: that `level` exists but simply holds no ERROR/FATAL values. The mapping lists no `level` property at all, and the severity values present in the documents live in integer field `severity_num` (3/4/5/6 for INFO/WARN/ERROR/FATAL).

For severity filtering in this index, query the integer field `severity_num` (ERROR=5, FATAL=6) or match the bracketed prefix in `msg`; if string severity values are wanted, an ingest pipeline or mapping change adding a keyword `level` field would be required — that is advice, not an action taken here.

Both count queries (0 hits for `level`, 8 hits for `severity_num`) ran in the tool's default 1-hour window ending 2026-11-23T18:09:28Z. The full-window aggregation shows all 23 docs of the index fall inside that hour, but documents deleted or outside retention are unknown, so 0 and 8 are window-and-retention-bounded counts, not guarantees about all log history.

The numeric meaning ERROR=5 / FATAL=6 is inferred from the corpus itself (msg prefixes in the returned documents), not from mapping metadata, which records only that `severity_num` is an integer; the field's declared help text was not available.
